quote_text:
Yeah, no, I thought… you say in the absence  of Lennon Miller, I say in the absence of  
a performance against Hearts. That was my  biggest point that I wanted to address today,  
and that was what the players wanted, too.  You know, it’s fine me saying that, but they  
were hurting a little bit, they were a bit sore  from the performance just a few days ago, and I  
just felt that they gave us that today right from  the word go. I thought we looked as if we were in  
connection with everything we were trying to do,  and obviously we scored a couple of good goals.
I addressed a bit where I think we can certainly  play better in the second half, and we can make  
that a lot easier for ourselves—take the threat  of Aberdeen away, spend more time on the ball  
with more control. But the biggest part for  me today was to get a reaction and to look  
to get three points, with the added bonus  of a clean sheet, which is great for us.
The red card didn’t happen just in front of you? A red card… well, at the time it looked as if  
there’s contact—it looked as if Rubežić jumps up  and makes contact with Tony. And I’ve actually  
just seen the television pictures there, which  confirm that as well. So, I don’t know that  
there’s much to contest there. I don’t think  you’ll get away with that reaction. We had a  
straight red card to Dan Casey for nothing like  that, which was obviously upheld, so, you know,  
you can say it’s a break or whatever. When we went  through this spell that we have done in the last  
number of weeks, you’ll understand I’m not going  to speak too much about it. I’ll just let it go,  
and I feel that it was probably justified.  I think the referee’s probably got it right.
I know he’s a player you said has  gone under the radar all season,  
but Jan Wilson’s first goal for the club and  just his general performance today—is that  
goal merited off the back of the season he’s had? Yeah, I’m delighted for him. He’s reached every  
kind of challenge that I’ve set him so far,  be it a couple of times playing in midfield,  
playing on the left-hand side, playing  against good players on a weekly basis,  
and all those learning points, all those learning  curves that come for a young player who might  
not have thought that he was going to find  himself in this position. But he’s embraced it.  
I feel that he carries a real threat  with his quality and his left foot,  
and we speak to him a lot about trying to get his  shot volume up because he has such control and  
such good technique that way. So I’m delighted  he finds himself in that position and has the  
composure to execute it. It’s obviously a big goal  in the game at that stage—to get the first one.
Again, coming on in particular, the reaction for  Cal Slattery coming on the park as well—did that  
put sort of a nice ending to the game? Yeah, I keep saying it: we’ve got a lot  
of good players there who are trying to find  their way back into full fitness—Sam Nicholson,  
Jack Wilkinson, Stephen O’Donnell, Paul McGinn,  Callum Slattery. The list kind of feels endless.  
But I don’t say it smugly; I know these guys  can play football. I know these guys can be  
very good players for this football club. So  I’m especially pleased to see some of them  
come back on the pitch and offer the quality  they have, the contribution they can give.
But I have to touch especially on Slattery.  When you’ve been out for that period of time  
with that kind of significant injury… we missed  a bounce game, as I said just the other day,  
which was a blow, but watching him in training—and  I don’t want to get carried away too much—but he’s  
just a lad that has such enthusiasm and such joy  in playing football, who has so much quality to  
bring. And so, you know, even at that stage in the  game today, I know he’s going to go in there and  
handle the ball, I know he’s going to go in there  with real enthusiasm. And as I said to the players  
in the dressing room, there’s always that human  touch on it. When somebody enjoys playing the game  
as much as he does, you’re just desperate, and  you love to see him getting back on the pitch.
Where did your yellow card stem  from—frustration with decisions? 
That’s probably what it comes down to, yeah.
Can you confirm there were two more reds  for coaches, either team, at half time? 
I believe there was a wee fracas in the  tunnel, which, for me, when you deal with  
competitors—and again, human beings—then that  type of thing may happen. I don’t actually  
know the ins and outs of it, because I  was in the dressing room at that point;  
I missed absolutely every part of it. So I know  that one of the coaching staff at Aberdeen was  
given a red, and I know Richard Foster was  given a red. That’s the situation. It’s not  
what we’re angling for; it’s not what we want.  But essentially, that was the fallout from it.
What can you say about Mikael Mandron’s  involvement in the first goal—he’s a  
brilliant assist for the second as well? He’s another one that’s a breath of fresh air.  
We didn’t feel that he turned up against Hearts.  There’s always a frustration when you know that  
he’s got so much quality, and I’m not pinning  that solely on him. It’s just that when you’re  
as good at handling the ball and you have that  creative brain, that quality… we want it every  
single week. We want to see that every single  opportunity. But remembering that he’s in the  
infancy of his senior career—he’s not played that  many senior games—and he’s having a good impact.  
I speak about the fact that I think he gives you  a threat playing between players and receiving  
the ball, but I also think he gives you that  threat with his pace, and a lot of people just  
lean to that. But he’s very clever—his change of  direction and how he handles the ball. He’s had  
a massive bearing on the game for us yet again  today, and he needs to continue that because the  
sky starts to become the limit, in my opinion, if  he can rack up the numbers with the performances.
Certainly no let-up in terms of  the intensity of the fixtures  
either—another 72 hours before the next one? No, we’ve managed to squeeze another one in there,  
which is great. It’s fine—that’s what it is,  coming into it off the back of a victory.  
You know, it’s a completely different game on  the astroturf against Kilmarnock, and we need  
to approach it differently. Potentially team  selection alters and shifts a little bit to  
make sure that everybody’s as fresh as they  can be. But it’s going to be a challenge;  
it’s going to be a tough old game against a team  that has a good home record on that surface and  
a team that’s currently—I don’t know what  the results are just now—but in really,  
really good form, Kilmarnock, and  generally have been since Derek’s  
been in charge as well. So I know what to  expect and what they can bring. For us,  
it’s to try and start the game the way we  did against Rangers, start the game the way  
we did against Aberdeen, and give ourselves  an opportunity in a difficult away fixture.
title: Stuart Kettlewell Post Match Press Conference | Motherwell 2-0 Aberdeen
